report.summary: Analyzed chunk 4 of 15 of correctness.py; checked docstring claims, public symbols, and observations.
risks: line 361-363 | medium | Docstring claims parse_pytest_output reduces several outcomes for one node to the worst of them; code does implement worst-wins ranking via _STATUS_RANK, but claim is uncheckable for the reporting behavior described. | Check that parse_pytest_output is called with output containing multiple lines for the same node and verify worst outcome is selected.

line 377-379 | medium | Docstring claims _STATUS_RANK prevents averaging; code shows ranking but claim about 'hiding a fatal blind spot' is interpretative and not directly checkable. | Verify that the ranking logic indeed prevents a single red case from being averaged away by green ones in practice.

line 396-398 | medium | Docstring claims missing nodes outrank everything because the node does not exist; code sets STATUS_MISSING last, so it overwrites previous statuses, consistent with claim. | Confirm that STATUS_MISSING is indeed the highest priority in downstream consumers.

line 446-448 | medium | Docstring claims output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree to avoid pipe deadlock; code does not show file output in this chunk. | Check the implementation of _spawn_pytest in later chunks to verify file output.
line 449-450 | medium | Claim that 'a quietly weaker containment that nobody can see is worse than a named one' is a design principle, not checkable in code. | N/A
todos: Verify that _spawn_pytest writes output to a file outside the worktree as claimed.
Check that the containment field is properly set in all code paths.

claims.text: Those report lines belong to the requested node (see :func:`parse_pytest_output`, which reduces several outcomes for one node to the WORST of them, so one red case cannot be averaged away by two green ones).
claims.why: The claim refers to parse_pytest_output's behavior; the code for parse_pytest_output is present and does implement worst-wins ranking via _STATUS_RANK, but the claim about 'report lines belonging to the requested node' refers to preceding context not in this chunk.

claims.text: A node the output says nothing about is ``not_run`` -- not a pass, not a fail.
claims.why: parse_pytest_output initializes statuses dict with STATUS_NOT_RUN for all requested nodes, and only changes status if a line matches.

claims.text: An explicit ``not found`` (``missing``) is final and outranks everything, because the node does not exist; otherwise several report lines for one node reduce to the WORST outcome seen (see ``_STATUS_RANK``); a node with no line of its own inherits ``collect_error`` if its FILE failed to collect.
claims.why: Code sets missing nodes to STATUS_MISSING last, overwriting previous statuses. Worst-wins ranking via _STATUS_RANK is applied in the loop. Nodes with no line but whose file is in file_errors get STATUS_COLLECT_ERROR.

claims.text: Preferred path is :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`, i.e. a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a hung or forking test tree dies with the run -- the same containment the repo's own pytest gate uses.
claims.why: The code chunk does not show the implementation of _spawn_pytest; it only shows the docstring. The actual use of ManagedProcess is not visible.

claims.text: If that backend is unavailable the run still happens through ``subprocess.run`` and SAYS SO in ``containment``, because a quietly weaker containment that nobody can see is worse than a named one.
claims.why: The code chunk does not show the implementation; the claim about setting containment field cannot be verified.

observations.what: The docstring for parse_pytest_output claims it reduces several outcomes to the worst; the code does implement worst-wins via _STATUS_RANK.
The missing nodes are processed last and overwrite previous statuses, ensuring finality as claimed.
The to_dict method sorts statuses by key, which may not preserve insertion order but is deterministic.
The _spawn_pytest docstring mentions ManagedProcess and subprocess.run fallback, but the implementation is not in this chunk.
The containment field in PytestRun is documented but not set in this chunk.
